english: The number of solutions of the equation $\tan\left(\pi\sin x\right)=1$ in the interval $[0,9\pi]$ is ______.
hindi: अन्तराल $[0,9\pi]$ में समीकरण $\tan\left(\pi\sin x\right)=1$ के हलों की संख्या ______ है।
solution: General solution of $\tan\theta=1$: $\theta=n\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}$, so $\pi\sin x=n\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}\Rightarrow\sin x=n+\frac14$
$|\sin x|\le1\Rightarrow n=0$ or $n=-1$: $\sin x=\frac14$ or $\sin x=-\frac34$ (not just the principal value $\frac{\pi}{4}$)
For these values $\pi\sin x\ne\pm\frac{\pi}{2}$, so $\tan(\pi\sin x)$ is defined
Each period $[2k\pi,2k\pi+2\pi)$: $\sin x=\frac14$ twice (in $(2k\pi,2k\pi+\pi)$), $\sin x=-\frac34$ twice, so $4$ solutions
solution_full: Let $\theta=\pi\sin x$; then $\theta\in[-\pi,\pi]$. The general solution of $\tan\theta=1$ is $\theta=n\pi+\frac{\pi}{4}$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$.
In $[-\pi,\pi]$ this gives $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ ($n=0$) and $\theta=-\frac{3\pi}{4}$ ($n=-1$). Taking only the principal value $\frac{\pi}{4}$ would miss the second family.
So $\sin x=\frac14$ or $\sin x=-\frac34$. For both, $\theta\ne\pm\frac{\pi}{2}$, so the tangent is defined.

In one period $[2k\pi,2k\pi+2\pi)$: $\sin x=\frac14$ has two solutions, both in $(2k\pi,2k\pi+\pi)$; $\sin x=-\frac34$ has two solutions, both in $(2k\pi+\pi,2k\pi+2\pi)$. That is $4$ solutions per period, none at the ends of a period.
On $[8\pi,9\pi]$, $\sin x\ge0$, so only $\sin x=\frac14$ contributes, with $2$ solutions; $\sin x=-\frac34$ contributes none.
originality_note: New: the general solution of tan theta = 1 is applied to theta = pi sin x, where the bound |sin x| <= 1 keeps exactly two members of the family (n = 0 and n = -1), and the count runs over a non-whole number of periods (way 5). Closest known: sin(pi cos x) = cos(pi sin x) type composite equations. Different because: here the second member n = -1 is the trap and the interval [0, 9pi] ends in mid-period.
blueprint_concepts: General solution of sin(x) = k, cos(x) = k, tan(x) = k

concept_use.General solution of sin(x) = k, cos(x) =: The general solution theta = n pi + pi/4 of tan theta = 1, and then the solutions of sin x = 1/4 and sin x = -3/4 counted period by period.
concept_use.Principal solution vs general solution: Using only the principal value pi/4 gives sin x = 1/4 alone (10 solutions); the general solution supplies the second value sin x = -3/4.
